title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 23
paragraphs: These are the cities that lie on Athos. They dug in this manner, the country having been divided among the barbarian nations for the job. Starting at the city of Sane, they drew a straight line across the isthmus. When the channel grew deep, those who were standing at the bottom dug, while others passed the earth upward to men above them, who in turn passed it on as if up a flight of steps, until it reached the men at the top, who carried it away and dumped it. All the nations except the Phoenicians had double labor, because the steep sides of their trench kept caving in — which was only to be expected, since they tried to make the opening at the top the same width as the one at the bottom. But the Phoenicians, who generally show cleverness in their work, showed it here as well: once their assigned portion had been allotted to them, they began digging by making the opening at the top twice as wide as the channel itself was to be, and then as the work advanced they kept narrowing it, so that at the bottom their trench came out the same width as the others'. A meadow lay nearby, and in it a market and trading-place was set up for the workmen, and great quantities of grain were brought to them regularly from Asia, already ground.
